newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - American dream.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - American dream.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN

U.S. insurer Cigna yesterday made its contribution to the global debate about funding retirement in the form of a report entitled "Coming of Age: The Economic & Political Impact of an Ageing Society."
America faces the same question as other developed economies -- how to fund people's higher material expectations in retirement at a time when life expectancy is generally rising?

The Cigna report, based on a survey of 18 to 32 year olds, found that 70 percent thought they should take most responsibility for funding their retirement years and would like to see tax incentives to save for this purpose.

"CIGNA found Baby Boomers want to be less dependent on Social Security and are ready to vote for change that would encourage all Americans to invest more in tax-deferred programs," said Byron D. Oliver, president of CIGNA Retirement & Investment Services.

"America can achieve the right political solutions to avoid bankrupting the Social Security system...only when our national retirement policy begins to encourage individual financial self-sufficiency through tax law change," he added.
The report also found that more than half expect to work beyond the normal retirement age of 65, either because they want to or will have to, but that many hanker after an early retirement.

Pension providers like Cigna have their part to play in helping people achieve their ambitions of early or phased retirement, but private schemes ignore the predicament of those without work or who cannot afford to save for retirement.

Cigna's survey, carried out with pollsters Harris, shows that, America, like other countries, has much work to do before agreeing a retirement income system that meets the expectations of all parties.
Insurers and other pension providers also tend to gloss over the fact that their recent track record in pension provision -- certainly in Britain and America -- has been littered with scandals.
